newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta quits NATO's Partnership for Peace.
newsitem.headline: Malta quits NATO's Partnership for Peace.

text.p: Malta has pulled out of NATO's Partnership for Peace Programme, Foreign Minister George Vella said on Tuesday night.
"Malta has already withdrawn," he told journalists less than three hours after being sworn in with the rest of the new cabinet in the Mediterranean island state.
Prime Minister Alfred Sant, 48, leader of the new Labour government elected on Saturday, told Reuters before the poll that leaving the Partnership for Peace would be his first priority."
Malta joined the Western alliance's programme of military cooperation last year under the outgoing Nationalist government of Edward Fenech Adami.
Labour has argued that increasingly frequent visits by Western naval vessels violated Malta's constitutional neutrality and could turn the small state back into a fortress island.
Vella also told journalists not to expect any dramatic moves on the country's application, which Labour pledged to scrap, to join the European Union.
He said the new government would stick to its manifesto, in which dismantling Value Added Tax (VAT) wass a major element, and this would preclude Malta's membership of the EU.
